description: Repository config on top of the shared preset github>thomas-lg-lab/renovate-config (schedule, dashboard, deps prefix, labels, squash, GitHub Actions groups). Translated from the former .github/dependabot.yml: same ecosystems, groups and ignores. No auto-merge: every merge to main publishes :latest.

packageRules.description: One PR for every NuGet minor and patch: a bump in Application or Infrastructure also rewrites the packages.lock.json of Api and Tests, which Renovate restores together (dotnet restore --force-evaluate on every dependent project).
Every base-image bump edits the same Dockerfile; ungrouped they conflict with each other one merge at a time (#67/#68, then #87/#88).
Pinned so a rebuild cannot silently change what every scan reads; the OCR benchmark in CI is the review.

The npm engine and packageManager in package.json are not dependency bumps: npm moves with an Angular upgrade. engines.node is not in here: it moves with the Node major (below), and a dependency disabled here could not be re-enabled by a rule that matches an update type, which only applies after lookup.

Microsoft.OpenApi 3.x makes IOpenApiMediaType.Example read-only, which the Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi source generator still assigns to (CS0200). Unblocked only by an ASP.NET Core release built against OpenApi 3.x. Listed in the Dependency Dashboard (Pending Approval); tick it to get the PR.

Angular pins TypeScript to a narrow peer range (@angular/build 22 wants >=6.0 <6.1): majors and minors move with an Angular upgrade, patches flow. Listed in the Dependency Dashboard (Pending Approval); tick it to get the PR.

@angular/build's unit-test builder declares peerOptional vitest@^4.0.8 through 22.1.x (#122). Drop this when 22.2 ships stable and move both together. Listed in the Dependency Dashboard (Pending Approval); tick it to get the PR.

Keep the Node references at major precision so they track the LTS line: docker versioning only proposes tags of the same shape (24-slim -> 26-slim), where the node versioning config:recommended applies would pin 26.13.0-slim.
engines.node lists every major Angular supports: a Node major adds to it rather than replacing it.

Node is one upgrade across the Dockerfile, the setup-node versions in the workflows, the devcontainer feature and engines in package.json (#92): one PR for all of them, reviewed, and CI checks the whole set. Angular's supported range decides when to merge it.

setup-node and the devcontainer feature say 24, which node versioning reads as 24.0.0: a minor would pin it to a full version and stop it tracking the LTS line, so nothing moves while it is a bare major. Once a full version is written (the Node major PR writes one), minor and patch flow again, so it keeps getting Node's security releases.
.NET is one upgrade across global.json, the setup-dotnet versions, the SDK, runtime and devcontainer images and the runtime-bound Microsoft.* packages: one PR for all of them, reviewed.

global.json is a floor, not a pin (rollForward latestFeature): the SDK that builds is whatever setup-dotnet, the SDK image and the devcontainer image carry, so raising the floor on every patch would only churn.
setup-dotnet's 10.0.x already follows the line; a patch would pin it to one SDK. Once a full version is written (the .NET major PR writes one), minor and patch flow again.
